scenes.text: It's night, and you can't see a thing.
So you light a fire in the middle of the room. Light! And smoke. So much smoke.
So you make a candle. Wax and a string. Way less smoke, but it is dim, it drips, and it is gone in a few hours.
So you burn oil inside a glass chimney. Brighter. But it stinks, and one bump could set your house on fire.
You need light with no flame. So you push electricity through a thin wire, until it gets so hot it glows.
For about two seconds. The air makes the hot wire burn right up.
So you seal the wire inside a glass bulb, and suck all the air out. Now it glows for hundreds of hours.
But most of the power turns into heat, not light. Touch it and you will find out.
So you swap the wire for a tiny chip that glows when electricity flows through it. An L E D.
Same light, a fraction of the power, and it lasts for years. Congratulations. You invented modern lighting.
